trigger: A readable live artifact contains `ARCHIVED`. The existing archived artifact contains `ARCHIVED UNIQUE SUFFIX`, has mode 000, and its parent is writable. The test first confirms a real `EACCES` reading it, then invokes the public `runGcCommand` archive path as the ordinary user.

closed_evidence: The original real mode-000/EACCES probe now returns archived=0 with EACCES and preserves `ARCHIVED UNIQUE SUFFIX`.
how_found_quote: The test first confirms a real `EACCES` reading it, then invokes the public `runGcCommand` archive path as the ordinary user.

title: nlink does not establish that the live path has a surviving directory entry
trigger: Make archive `a` and `b` hard links to one inode (`nlink=2`); make live `a` and `b` symlinks to those archive names.
measured: restore returns `artifactsRestored:true`, `notRestored:[]`; all four paths become unreadable (`copies:[null,null,null,null]`). The last two real links were both inside the tree it deleted. This is a static filesystem configuration, not a race.
closed_evidence: Original static multilink reproduction preserves bytes; ordinary same-inode restore now refuses before either old late-hook can run. Actual directory bind mounts are refused in both directions.
how_found_quote: Make archive `a` and `b` hard links to one inode (`nlink=2`); make live `a` and `b` symlinks to those archive names.

title: The record fallback bypasses transcript classification and discards opaque bytes
trigger: `r4-safety.test.ts`, the opaque-shape matrix and `empty archived artifact cannot consume divergent title-only content`.
measured:
- A nonempty artifact consisting only of a canonical title slot is skipped to EOF by `nextRecord`; `recordsAreCarried` returns true before requiring any header. Restore deletes it even when the live file is unrelated content of sufficient length.
- Noncanonical short title lines and title-shaped records later in a file are skipped too. The canonical-width/opening-position contract is not enforced in this fallback.
- An ordinary `tool-output.log` starting `{"type":"session","id":"example","title":...}` is treated as a transcript. Changing its title field discards the archive's unique bytes in both archive and restore directions.
how_found_quote: In these restore probes the operation reports complete success and removes the archive.

title: Staging and a final stat pass do not protect the named publication/deletion races
trigger: `r4-safety.test.ts` and `extra.test.ts`, using deterministic hooks to perform real filesystem mutations at the boundaries required by the assignment.
measured:
- Replace the destination after staging/comparison but before `rename`: both archive and restore overwrite `NEW USER WORK` with `ORIGINAL` and report success.
- Replace the source after staging: both paths remove the newer `NEW WORK` source and retain only the staged `ORIGINAL`.
- Change an earlier restored file from `UNIQUE` to same-length `OTHER!` while a later file is published: the final pass checks size/inode, not carried content; it deletes the archive's `UNIQUE`.
- A live hard link changed into an archive-pointing symlink changes actual `nlink` from 2 to 1. Before the final pass it is caught. At the subsequent `fs.rm` boundary it is not: restore reports success and both paths vanish.
how_found_quote: A live hard link changed into an archive-pointing symlink changes actual `nlink` from 2 to 1.

title: The archive-side fallback reads a descriptor already closed by its fast path
trigger: `archived.createReadStream({start:0})` uses automatic close. After the byte comparison fails, `linesOfHandle(archived)` is called on the closed descriptor; the catch turns this into false.
measured: direct probe prints `ARCHIVED_FALLBACK {"carries":false,"fd":-1}` for a record-preserving addition of usage fields. The public reproduction in `extra.test.ts` uses a real SessionManager rename on a legacy child and then rearchives its parent: `archived:0` with an incorrect `does not hold its bytes` error. Data remains, but valid recovery/rearchive is refused.
how_found_quote: The public reproduction in `extra.test.ts` uses a real SessionManager rename on a legacy child and then rearchives its parent
